title: A Summit for the Wreck
premise: Ines Halloran, a disgraced mountain guide hiding in a border town, is hired by a desperate woman named Mara Voss to find her father's expedition, which vanished while mapping the headwaters of the Rio Sombra—a river whose source lies inside a valley closed by treaty and haunted by an old mining disaster. Following the river upstream, Ines uncovers that the expedition was searching for the mine's lost survey records, which prove his own late mentor falsified the route maps that caused the disaster and Ines's blacklisting. At the frozen source, Ines finds two survivors of the expedition and must choose between destroying the records to protect his mentor's memory or bringing them down to clear his name at the cost of Mara's inheritance. He brings them down whole, testifies to the truth, and walks out of the valley neither innocent nor exiled—finally free because he stopped running.
about_author: Rosalind Winterbourne is a former river-boat cook who spent a decade drifting between port towns before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people the maps forgot, from a houseboat moored somewhere she refuses to disclose.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot His Name
chapters.summary: Ines Halloran works odd jobs in Puerto Ceniza, keeping his head down after being blacklisted from guiding in two countries. When a woman named Mara Voss arrives asking for him by name, he realizes his anonymity has already been sold. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: wary dread—the past has found him.

chapters.title: A Debt With Teeth
chapters.summary: Mara offers Ines money he can't refuse: her father Emil's expedition up the Rio Sombra stopped answering its radio nine days ago, and the authorities won't enter the closed valley. Ines recognizes the debt collector shadowing Mara and understands refusal means ruin. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: cornered resignation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines gathers gear and an old partner, Tomás, who owes him a life. Locals warn that the upper Sombra swallowed a mining town in '61 and that the treaty closing the valley exists for good reason. Ines studies his dead mentor Aldous Rennick's old route maps and notices something altered. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: unease seeded beneath competence.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: The trio launches by boat through gorges where the radio crackles with static shaped almost like voices. They find the expedition's abandoned supply cache—opened carefully, not looted—and a journal page pinned under a stone: coordinates, and the word WRONG circled twice. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the hunt begins; excitement laced with foreboding.

chapters.title: The First Grave
chapters.summary: They discover a fresh grave marked with Emil Voss's ice axe but no body. Tomás wants to turn back; Ines finds drag marks leading uphill instead of downstream. That night someone steals their fuel and leaves a strip of expedition flagging tape in exchange. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion—they are being managed, not attacked.

chapters.title: Mara's Version
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: Mara's POV in Puerto Ceniza, revealing she hired Ines not only for rescue but because her father's last letter mentioned 'Rennick's lie' and named Ines as the only guide who might understand it. Emotional beat: Mara's guilt—she may have sent her father to his death chasing her family's name.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Portaging the falls, Tomás nearly drowns and confesses he was paid by the debt collectors to report Ines's position. Ines spares him but strips him of trust. The group fractures just as they cross the invisible treaty line into the closed valley. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: betrayal, loneliness, and the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Valley That Was Closed on Purpose
chapters.summary: Inside the valley, the forest is wrong—too quiet, terraced with ruins of the drowned mining town exposed by drought. Ines finds the old mine adit sealed with modern bolts. Fresh boot prints everywhere, none leaving. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: awe and violation; they've entered someone's secret.

chapters.title: Voices on the Static
chapters.summary: At night the stolen radio transmits on its own frequency: a repeating loop of Emil Voss's voice giving coordinates. Mara insists it's a message; Ines suspects bait. They follow it anyway, into a fog-filled gorge where the temperature drops without reason. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion.

chapters.title: The Survey Hut
chapters.summary: They reach a hidden hut containing the 1961 original survey—Rennick's handwriting all over it, with corrections proving the official route map was falsified to hide an unstable shaft, the same falsification that later damned Ines. Someone has been living here. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: vertigo of revelation—his disgrace was engineered.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stayed
chapters.summary: They're found by Silas Brandt, Emil's chief surveyor, half-starved and armed. He reveals Emil is alive, injured, sheltering higher up—but Brandt refuses to let the survey leave the valley, believing its publication will reopen the mine and kill more people. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: confrontation between two men both protecting ghosts.

chapters.title: Emil Voss, Alive and Unforgiving
chapters.summary: Reunion at a high camp: Emil, leg shattered, has spent weeks verifying every line of the survey. He tells Mara the truth—that her grandfather owned the mine and helped bury the disaster's cause. Mara's inheritance is built on the lie. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: shattering of family myth; love tested against truth.

chapters.title: Three Versions of One Night
chapters.summary: Interleaved testimonies—Ines, Brandt, Emil—reconstruct the night of the original disaster and the night Rennick burned the evidence, using Ines as scapegoat. Each version is true and incomplete. POV: rotating. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—memory is a survival tool and a weapon.

chapters.title: The Debt Collectors Arrive
chapters.summary: Helicopter noise: the men behind Mara's debt have tracked them, hired by interests who want the valley reopened and the survey destroyed or seized. A standoff at the high camp goes wrong; Tomás, returned to make amends, takes a bullet meant for Ines. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: guilt renewed—the price of dragging others upstream.

chapters.title: Descent Is Not Retreat
chapters.summary: With Tomás dying and weather closing in, Ines proposes carrying everyone down through the unclimbed gorge—the route Rennick falsified, which Ines alone has memorized correctly. Brandt resists; Emil overrules him. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership; the guide reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Route That Killed Them
chapters.summary: The descent through the gorge becomes a gauntlet of rockfall and rising water. Ines navigates by the corrected survey lines, literally walking his mentor's lie backward. They lose the supplies but not each other. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: catharsis through mastery—the map finally telling the truth under his feet.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Forced off-route, they emerge at the river's true source: a glacial spring above the drowned mine, where the 1961 flood began. Here Ines must decide—burn the survey as Brandt demands, or carry it out. Mara chooses truth over inheritance and sides with Ines. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm; choice made.

chapters.title: What Brandt Carried
chapters.summary: Brandt's backstory breaks open: he lost his family in the '61 flood and stayed twenty years guarding the valley from reopening. Confronted with Emil's verified pages, he realizes silence protected no one. He surrenders the survey but asks to be the one who testifies first. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: grief converted into purpose.

chapters.title: Running the Drowned Town
chapters.summary: Climax begins: the debt collectors' second team floods the valley to seize the survey and silence witnesses. A chase through the ruined mining town as the river rises from upstream meltwater. Ines uses the falsified route against the pursuers, sealing them in the old adit—nonlethally. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: ferocity in defense of truth.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Out of the valley, the survivors face officials, journalists, and the debt holders. Brandt testifies; the survey's authenticity is confirmed; the blacklisting of Ines is formally reversed and the mine permanently closed by amended treaty. Mara renounces her tainted inheritance publicly. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: vindication that feels like loss and relief at once.

chapters.title: Burials
chapters.summary: Tomás survives, broken but honest. They bury Rennick's falsified maps beside the grave on the riverbank—giving the mentor a truth he never gave anyone. Ines and Mara part at the dock, her debt dissolved, his name restored, neither sure what comes next. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: mourning, gratitude, tenderness held loosely.

chapters.title: A Summit for the Wreck
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, Ines takes his first legitimate commission—guiding a small scientific team to document the source now that the valley is legally accessible. At the spring, he leaves his old compass, the one Rennick gave him, pointing home. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; the wreck salvaged, the summit reached, the man no longer hiding.
